source.paper: Four-Coloring P6-Free Graphs. II. Finding an Excellent Precoloring
source.audited_object: Lemma 11 state interface from Q_{T,T'} through P_{Q,f'} and equivalence construction

local_index.object: (T,T') from the fixed set of ordered type-pairs with singleton distinct f(T),f(T')

consumers: membership in the enumerated family Q

support_interface.global_support: S(Q)=union over all type-pairs of V(Q_{T,T'})
consumers: Y0 update by removing S(Q) and N(S(Q))

admissibility_interface.z_forcing_left_or_right: depending on which Y(type) contains local Z, f'(Z) is forced to the opposite singleton seed color specified in the paper
admissibility_interface.middle_color_rule: no separate explicit color restriction beyond membership in the proper coloring of S union S(Q) union X0 union Z(Q)
admissibility_interface.global_properness: f union f' must be proper on G induced by S union S(Q) union X0 union Z(Q)

subcase_interface.construction: P_{Q,f'} uses seed S union S(Q), precolored X0 union Z(Q), original X, transformed Y0/Y, and coloring f union f'
required_properties: is a normal subcase of P
subcase_interface.hidden_connectivity_obligation: S union S(Q) must be connected. Legacy endpoint representatives lie in Y and have seed-neighbors; a nonempty middle representative is adjacent to an endpoint, thereby attaching it to the enlarged seed.

complexity_interface.admissible_color_bound: at most 4^|S(Q)| support precolorings; the paper states each support precoloring extends to an admissible function in a unique way
complexity_interface.consequence: bounded local support and deterministic/controlled Z-color semantics are part of the proof interface, not merely implementation details

reconstruction_interface.soundness_side: a member produced from P_{Q,f'} is a normal-subcase descendant, and extensions reconstruct to P through the established normal-subcase/Lemma-10 chain
reconstruction_interface.completeness_side: for a fixed extension c, each type-pair is assigned one of the three legacy patterns and corresponding f' values; the resulting Q,f' must be among the enumerated candidates

R3_MINIMAL_NEW_INTERFACE.note: This is an abstract interface contract only. It intentionally does not define a concrete SPLIT state or transition algorithm.

local_state_must_expose.meaning: finite mode identifier sufficient to distinguish legacy patterns and any future rigid-corridor extension
bounded set P subseteq Y(T), legacy arity <=1
bounded set N subseteq Y(T'), legacy arity <=1
bounded set C subseteq Y0 replacing the hard-coded legacy middle M at interface level
explicit/verifiable adjacency and nonadjacency relations among endpoints and attachment carrier sufficient to validate local-state membership; legacy COMMON requires C complete to P union N

proof-carrying or polynomially checkable witness that the local mode satisfies its declared graph/seed conditions; a future rigid-corridor mode must bind to P7_CORRIDOR_RIGIDITY rather than trust a label
bounded subset A(state) of stored vertices promoted into S(Q)
deterministic polynomial-time local rule/predicate defining Z_state from G, the type-pair and local state
constraints on f' over support and Z, including endpoint exclusions, any carrier constraints, forced Z values, and the global proper-coloring obligation
produces exactly the data consumed by the normal-subcase formula: support S(Q), Z(Q), and f'
a polynomially checkable map obligation showing how a fixed original extension c selects this local state and compatible color data
exact reverse semantic obligation from generated descendants to the original P
constant/bounded number of stored vertex identities per type-pair, finite mode alphabet, polynomial membership/Z evaluation, and polynomially bounded admissible color choices

cross_cutting_obligations.NORMAL_SUBCASE_CONNECTIVITY: The interface must prove S union S(Q) connected for every admitted local mode; this cannot be delegated to a post-hoc solver.
cross_cutting_obligations.POLYNOMIAL_BUDGET: The interface must expose enough bounds to re-derive n^{q(|S|)} enumeration and admissible-color counts. Semantic correctness without polynomial discoverability is insufficient.
cross_cutting_obligations.Z_DETERMINISM_OR_BOUNDED_BRANCHING: The old proof's counting uses that support precoloring determines the admissible values on Z uniquely. Any replacement must prove an equally polynomial bound; this audit does not assume uniqueness for a future mode.

intentionally_unresolved: whether both rigid-corridor Y0 attachments belong in support_projection
whether a future rigid-corridor mode has Z_state=empty
what colors must be stored/guessed for multiple attachment carriers
whether corridor seed vertices need to be stored or merely certified/derived
whether one future mode is sufficient or multiple local modes are required

R4_CONSERVATIVE_EMBEDDING.abstract_embedding: iota maps every legacy Q_{T,T'}=(P,M,N) to a new-interface state with legacy mode tag, identical P and N roles, attachment_carrier=M, legacy incidence contract, support_projection=P union M union N, and the exact original Z/color policies.

111.membership: z in Y0; z complete to P union N; P anticomplete N
111.color_semantics: exactly original endpoint restrictions plus global properness

001.color_semantics: exactly original endpoint and forced-Z rules

preservation_laws: For every legacy local state q, support_projection(iota(q)) = V(q).
For every legacy q, Z_selector(iota(q)) = original Z(T,T').
For every legacy tuple Q, union support under iota equals original S(Q).
For every legacy tuple Q, union Z under iota equals original Z(Q).
The set of admissible f' functions for iota(Q) is identical to the original Q-admissible set.
For every legacy Q,f', the constructed P_{iota(Q),f'} is byte-for-definition identical to original P_{Q,f'}.
The legacy local-support bound remains <=3 and the original n^{3t}, 4^{3t}-style counting argument is unchanged up to constant-size mode metadata.
Legacy completeness and reconstruction witnesses are not altered.
R4_CONSERVATIVE_EMBEDDING.limitation: No embedding is claimed for a future rigid-corridor state because such a state is intentionally not defined.

key_new_findings.finding: The old Q interface has a hidden fifth consumer: polynomial accounting.
key_new_findings.significance: A state extension that preserves semantics but loses bounded local support or controlled Z-color extension does not preserve the polynomial proof.

key_new_findings.finding: Normal-subcase connectivity is an interface obligation.
key_new_findings.significance: The new state must guarantee connectivity of S union S(Q), not merely define representatives and colors.

key_new_findings.finding: The future rigid-corridor Z semantics is genuinely unresolved.
key_new_findings.significance: Legacy 111 implies Z=empty by definition, but a two-attachment extension cannot inherit that branch without a new completeness/soundness proof.

key_new_findings.finding: Downstream P_{Q,f'} construction is factored through the projections S(Q), Z(Q), and f'.
key_new_findings.significance: A replacement state language need not preserve the literal triple syntax internally if it can provide these projections and all semantic/budget obligations exactly; however the completeness and acceptability proofs still require role-level data.

result.summary: R1-R4 are closed as a specification audit. The minimum future language must expose role membership/incidence, support projection, Z semantics, admissibility/color constraints, subcase projection, completeness/reconstruction bindings, connectivity, and polynomial budget. The legacy Q schema embeds conservatively by identity. No concrete rigid-corridor/SPLIT semantics has been defined or tested.
